items.description: On February 2, 2027, we will retire Azure Fluid Relay. After this date, Azure Fluid Relay will reach end of availability, and workloads that continue to depend on the service may experience disruption.The Fluid Framework remains available as an open-source framework for building distributed, real-time collaborative web applications. A self-hosted Fluid service solution is available as the replacement. You can continue using Azure Fluid Relay until February 1, 2027 while you complete your transition.How this affects you:If your applications continue to use Azure Fluid Relay after February 2, 2027, they may experience service disruption. Moving to the self-hosted solution means that you will be responsible for hosting and operating the Fluid service in your environment. Operational and infrastructure costs will depend on your deployment architecture, scale, and operational requirements.What you need to do:Transition workloads that depend on Azure Fluid Relay to a self-hosted Fluid service solution before February 2, 2027. Review your Azure subscriptions and identify applications that use Azure Fluid Relay, plan and complete the transition, and use the self-hosted Fluid service solution in the Fluid Framework GitHub repository as the migration and replacement resource.
items.title: Retirement: Azure Fluid Relay

items.description: You now have greater flexibility in network design for Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server workloads. Now you can change existing VNet-integrated servers from delegated-subnet networking to a private endpoint-capable configuration, enabling secure access over a private IP address through Azure Private Link. The migration retains existing backups; however, you should plan for a temporary connectivity interruption and configure a private endpoint or appropriate firewall rules after migration. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Change from virtual network integration to a private endpoint capable network configuration in Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server

items.description: This is the formal notice that Microsoft plans to deprecate the operational technology (OT) security component of Microsoft Defender for IoT. The service will be fully deprecated in October 2029, following a three-year transition period.This change applies only to Defender for IoT OT Security. Enterprise IoT capabilities in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint are not affected. Device discovery and vulnerability assessment will continue to be available.When this will happenDeprecation is planned for October 2029. This notice begins the transition period and does not require you to immediately stop using your existing deployment. Complete your migration to an alternative OT security solution before retirement.How this will affect your organizationIf you use Defender for IoT OT Security, you will need to transition to an alternative solution before October 2029. During the transition, the service will remain supported with routine security updates and bug fixes, but no new OT-specific capabilities or feature investments will be introduced. Existing customer agreements and renewals will be honored through October 2029.What you can do to prepareAssess your environment. Review existing OT deployments, sensors, integrations, licenses, contracts, and security requirements.Evaluate your options. Select an OT security solution that meets your organization’s needs. Microsoft offers connectors for Armis, Dragos, and Forescout, but you are not required to use a specific provider. OT data connectors in Microsoft Security Exposure Management support these three providers.Understand Microsoft integrations. Supported third-party OT connectors can bring OT asset and vulnerability data into Microsoft Security Exposure Management and the Defender portal.  Third-party solutions require separate licensing and deployment.Build your transition plan. Account for procurement, testing, operational validation, continuity, data export, and sensor decommissioning, with migration completed before October 2029.Engage early. Contact OT security providers directly or work with your Microsoft account team to help coordinate an introduction.Learn more:OT data connectors Data connectors overview Enterprise IoT
items.title: Retirement: OT security in Microsoft Defender for IoT

items.description:
Application Gateway for Containers now supports centralized
JSON Web Token validation through the AuthPolicy custom resource. Teams can
validate a token signature, issuer, lifetime, and configured audience by using
signing keys retrieved from a trusted HTTPS JSON Web Key Set endpoint. Requests
with missing or invalid credentials are rejected at the gateway instead of
being forwarded to the backend. AuthPolicy can protect an ApplicationLoadBalancer, Gateway,
HTTPRoute, GRPCRoute, or MCPRoute. Policies inherit through the resource
hierarchy, while a more specific route-level policy can replace an inherited
policy or explicitly opt a route out. Optional OAuth Protected Resource
Metadata helps OAuth-aware clients discover authorization servers and supported
scopes. Apply consistent JWT
validation to HTTP, gRPC, and MCP routes 
 Use
     Microsoft Entra ID or third-party identity providers that publish trusted
     JWKS signing keys 
 Combine
     JWT validation with WAF so malicious traffic is inspected before
     authentication 
 Publish
     OAuth resource metadata to enable authorization server discovery Learn more: JWT validation for Application Gateway
for Containers Configure JWT validation for
Application Gateway for Containers - Gateway API
items.title: Public Preview: JWT validation for Application Gateway for Containers

items.description:
Application Gateway for Containers now supports Model
Context Protocol routing through the new MCPRoute custom resource. Platform
teams can publish MCP servers behind a stable hostname and path while
centralizing TLS, JWT validation, Web Application Firewall protection, backend
health monitoring, and routing policy at the gateway. MCPRoute supports both direct routing to a single MCP
server and aggregation of multiple independent servers behind one logical
endpoint. For aggregated deployments, Application Gateway for Containers merges
tool, resource, and prompt discovery responses, namespaces capability names to
avoid collisions, and routes invocations to the backend that owns the selected
capability. Expose one governed
endpoint for MCP clients and Kubernetes-hosted MCP servers Aggregate capabilities from
multiple MCP servers  Session affinity for MCP
servers that maintain in-memory session state Apply JWT validation, WAF,
backend TLS, health checks, and cross-namespace references Learn more: Model Context Protocol capabilities in
Application Gateway for Containers Configure Model Context Protocol
routing for Application Gateway for Containers
items.title: Public Preview: MCP gateway for Application Gateway for Containers

items.description:
Application
Gateway for Containers now supports private frontends that are reachable only
through approved Azure Private Link private endpoints. This enables
organizations to keep internal applications, shared services, and cross-cluster
traffic on private connectivity while retaining Kubernetes-native Layer 7
routing, TLS, health probing, and Web Application Firewall capabilities. Private ingress supports connectivity across virtual
networks, subscriptions, Microsoft Entra tenants, and Azure regions without
requiring VNet peering. A single Application Gateway for Containers resource
can also host public and private frontends, allowing teams to use separate
exposure models and security policies for different workloads. Remove the public IP
address and direct internet path from the frontend Enforce access through
explicitly provisioned and approved private endpoints  Connect workloads across VNets, subscriptions,
tenants, and regions, including environments with overlapping CIDR ranges  Place an Azure Firewall,
network virtual appliance, or another upstream service in front of Kubernetes
workloads Learn more:   Private ingress with Application
Gateway for Containers  Configure private ingress
with Application Gateway for Containers - Gateway API
items.title: Public Preview: Private ingress for Application Gateway for Containers

items.description:
Azure
Migrate now supports discovery and assessment for network-attached storage,
allowing customers and partners to plan migrations of Dell PowerScale (OneFS)
and NetApp ONTAP storage to Azure. The Azure Migrate appliance connects
directly to your NAS clusters using read-only credentials, inventories every
SMB, NFS, and S3 share, and evaluates each share against Azure Files, Azure
Blob Storage, and Azure NetApp Files. Key benefits include: Discover Dell PowerScale/Isilon and NetApp ONTAP/FAS clusters
and the shares they host Group, tag, and filter NAS shares alongside your existing
server, application, and database inventory Assess each share with readiness, a right-sized Azure target
configuration, and monthly cost estimates Generate a business case comparing Azure storage services
against on-premises cost, and sequence moves using wave plans This capability replaces manual, spreadsheet-driven
NAS planning with a verified per-share inventory and a defensible cost basis,
especially for large or multi-protocol storage estates. NAS
is often the largest and least-understood part of an on-premises estate.
Bringing NAS discovery and assessment into Azure Migrate means storage is
planned in the same project, and the same business case, as the servers and
applications that depend on it. Getting started: To
get started, update your Azure Migrate appliance, add your NAS cluster as a
discovery source, and run an assessment directly from the Azure portal. Write to us at azurestoragemigrations@microsoft.com with questions or feedback. Learn
more.
items.title: Public Preview: On-prem NAS share discovery and assessment are now available using Azure Migrate

items.description: You can now restart or fail over databases directly from the Azure portal, including single databases, Hyperscale databases, and databases in elastic pools, without writing scripts against the Rest API or contacting support.  Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Restart databases in Azure SQL DB via the Azure portal

items.description:
Azure Storage Actions is introducing three enhancements to simplify task management and give you more control over automated data operations across Azure Blob and Data Lake Storage:Automatic propagation of task definition updates: When you update a storage task definition the changes now automatically apply to its existing assignments. Scheduled assignment runs use the updated definition on their next run, keeping your data management logic consistent without updating each assignment individually.Stop in-progress task assignment runs: You can request a stop for an individual task assignment’s in-progress run or across all assignments associated with a storage task. This gives you greater control when a run needs to be interrupted. Stop requests are processed asynchronously.Case-sensitive operators: Target data more precisely with case-sensitive variants of `equals`, `contains`, `startsWith`, `endsWith`, and `matches` string operators. These additional operators provide you more flexibility, helping you select the intended blobs when capitalization matters. Existing operators retain their case-insensitive behavior.Learn
more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Storage Actions adds automatic task updates, execution controls, and case-sensitive matching

items.description: Advanced capacity insights are now available for preview in Azure Storage Discovery. Storage Discovery now provides greater visibility into storage usage through insights such as access patterns, data age, storage tiers, object size distribution, retention states, and versioning. With these insights, teams can identify opportunities, understand factors contributing to storage growth, and inform storage management decisions at scale.Learn more:Discover what's new with advanced capacity insightsExplore advanced capacity insights and capabilitiesGet started with Azure Storage Discovery
items.title: Public Preview: Advanced capacity insights are now available in Azure Storage Discovery

items.description: Azure Site Recovery now offers an enhanced disaster recovery experience for virtual machines in Virtual Machine Scale Sets with flexible orchestration. The update improves target configuration and end-to-end recovery workflows, including failover, reprotection, and failback.Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Enhanced Azure Site Recovery support for VMSS Flex

items.description: Route maps for Azure Route Server are now generally available in the Azure public cloud. Route maps provide fine-grained control over inbound and outbound routing across hybrid connections. Customers can manage routes advertised to and from Azure Route Server BGP peerings with Network Virtual Appliances (NVAs), ExpressRoute gateways, and VPN gateways in the same virtual network. Route maps provide the following capabilities: Route summarization: Summarize routes when on-premises networks connect to the virtual network through ExpressRoute or VPN. Route control: Control routes entering and leaving Azure Route Server between on-premises networks, NVAs, and virtual networks. Path selection: Modify BGP attributes such as AS-PATH to make routes more or less preferred. Route tagging: Tag routes by using the BGP Community attribute.Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Route maps for Azure Route Server

items.description:
Geo-Replication on partitioned namespaces for
Azure Service Bus Premium is now generally available. You can now combine the
throughput benefits of partitioning with the reliability of replicating your
messages and metadata to a secondary Azure region. Partitioned namespaces distribute queues and topics across
multiple message brokers and messaging stores within a region, allowing
throughput to scale beyond a single broker. You can enable Geo-Replication on an existing partitioned
Premium namespace or configure both capabilities on a new namespace. Learn
more.
items.title: Generally Available: Geo-Replication on partitioned namespaces for Azure Service Bus Premium

items.description:
Azure Site Recovery support for Azure Local is now generally available, making enterprise-grade disaster recovery simpler, accessible, easier to setup and secure than ever before. Customers can protect supported Windows and Linux virtual machines by replicating workloads to Azure, extending their disaster recovery capabilities to the cloud.With streamlined setup in the Azure portal, customers can validate their recovery plans without disrupting production replication, fail over to Azure during planned or unplanned outages, and return workloads to Azure Local when their on-premises environment is ready. The capability is available in all Azure Local-supported regions.Learn more: Tech
Community blog Official
documentation
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Site Recovery for Azure Local

items.description: Multi-disk crash-consistent restore points for Azure virtual machines with Premium SSD v2 and Ultra data disks are now available in public preview on VMs with SCSI disk controllers. You can use this to capture the agent-less crash consistent restore point of a VM.This preview extends existing multi-disk crash-consistent restore point support to Premium SSD v2 and Ultra data disks. Existing support for Standard HDD, Standard SSD, and Premium SSD disks is unchanged.Instant Access is also supported for multi-disk crash-consistent restore points in this preview. This applies only to VMs with Premium SSD v2 and Ultra data disks. With Instant Access, you can begin restoring a disk as soon as the restore point is created instead of waiting for the background data copy to complete, helping reduce your recovery time objective.How to use itSet consistencyMode to CrashConsistent when creating a restore point in a restore point collection. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Multi-disk crash-consistent VM restore points for Premium SSD v2 and Ultra Disks on VMs with SCSI disk controller

items.description:
The Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server REST API version 2026-10-01 is now generally available. This stable API release introduces expanded capabilities for maintenance management, immutable backups, multi-tenant encryption (cross-tenant customer-managed keys (**CMKs**), Federal Information Processing Standards (**FIPS**) configuration, network migration, Premium SSD v2 storage, and major version upgrade prechecks. It also enhances autonomous tuning recommendations and introduces more flexible PostgreSQL version handling.These enhancements enable customers to automate more server management operations, strengthen security, and streamline database administration through a stable, production-ready API.Learn
more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Database for PostgreSQL stable REST API version 2026-10-01

items.description:
With this enhancement, you have the ability to lock your retention to the configured PITR retention, beyond the default 7 days of immutable backups that are already available. This is especially useful for financial customers who typically have 35 days of PITR retention. The current default immutability is up to 7 days, and with this enhancement you can extend and lock immutability up to 35 days.Once locked, only extensions to PITR retention are allowed. This setting is permanent for the life of the database.Learn
more.
items.title: Public Preview: Extend immutability for PITR backups for Azure SQL Database and Azure SQL Managed Instance

items.description:
Azure Firewall now supports application rules in IPv6
Public Preview, enabling layer 7 filtering for IPv6 HTTP and HTTPS traffic. The
enhancement extends application-level controls to IPv6 and dual-stack
deployments, helping customers maintain consistent policies across IPv4 and
IPv6 environments.Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Azure Firewall IPv6 now supports application rules
